design.title: Whole-frame receptive field: two extra stride-2 stages take the trunk from a 31 m texture window to the full 128 m frame, so the classifier can read street-and-block layout instead of an average of local textures
design.eli5: Until now the model looked at each 128-metre-wide aerial frame through 64 small 31-metre peepholes and then averaged what it saw, so all it could remember about a place was its mix of textures and colours: so much roof, so much asphalt, so much tree, in these tints. That is exactly the stuff that changes between two photographs of the same streets taken in different seasons, and the previous experiment deliberately scrambled it, which left the model with almost nothing to hold on to. This experiment widens its view to the whole frame at once, so it can finally see how the roads, blocks and water are arranged relative to each other, which is the same in every photograph of Berlin ever taken. The extra two layers are cheap and the exported model still fits the drone's memory.
design.hypothesis: Experiment 4 closed the exposure/sharpness route and the model did exactly what its architecture permits: it got much worse on its OWN training photographs (train_capture_diagnostics 0.060 / 0.053 / 0.088 -> 0.733 / 0.673 / 0.518, usable 94-96% -> 36-54%) while the held-out 2024 photograph improved only to 1.271 (usable 11.8%, false fix 38.8%), with training loss still falling steeply at epoch 8 (4.08, augmented top1 0.45 vs 0.79 before). The pre-registered hope was that capacity would 'move to the layout structure at 2 m scale and up that all four surveys share'. It cannot, because the trunk cannot see layout. Measured at design time on the current model (runs/_probe_exp5_rf.py, no training): the feature extractor is four 3x3 stride-2 convs, so each of the 8x8 = 64 positions of its final map has a receptive field of 31 x 31 px, i.e. 31 m of a 128 m frame, and global average pooling then averages those 64 local descriptors. The 160-d vector the 2,970-way classifier reads is therefore, by construction, a BAG OF 31 m TEXTURE PATCHES with all relative arrangement discarded: it can encode 'how much roof, asphalt, canopy, water of which tint and grain', but not 'a canal bends past a block of three courtyards with a wide road to the north'. The first is exactly what differs between a summer DOP20, a leaf-off 2022 and an early-spring 2023 survey (and what experiment 4 now randomises away); the second is what all four surveys share. With texture statistics randomised and arrangement unrepresentable, the model is left fitting whatever colour-and-grain statistics survive the augmentation, which is why it now underfits even its training photographs and why its mean_max_softmax is only 0.19. This is the one inference stage no experiment in this era has questioned: arch_json for experiments 2-4 carries changed:true only on 'Training signal' (and experiment 3's feature-consistency term), never on 'Feature extractor', and the trunk itself is byte-for-byte the mission-era one (chans [3,32,64,128,160], unchanged since commit 92d1f12). Extending the pyramid by two more stride-2 stages (8x8 -> 4x4 -> 2x2) takes the receptive field to 127 px, so every descriptor the pooling averages sees the whole frame and can represent arrangement; the two stages are depthwise-separable so they cost 55k parameters (+221 kB, 3.30 MB exported, under the 4 MiB gate) and negligible compute at 4x4 and 2x2 resolution. The earlier-era record contains 'tripled trunk depth made things worse' (four-area era experiments 26/28, pretrained MobileNetV3 on never-seen ground under a median metric) - that verdict is void here and asked a different question; this is a from-scratch trunk on fully-mapped ground, and the change is to receptive field, not to parameter count. Rotation remains the only geometric augmentation, so the pooled whole-frame descriptor still has to be learned rotation-invariant, as the texture one was.
